st.headline: Singlife to phase out Singlife Account insurance savings plan by end-2027
st.teaser: The move does not affect customers who hold other insurance policies.
fullText: SINGAPORE – Home-grown insurer Singlife will discontinue its savings and insurance product Singlife Account, with all remaining accounts to be closed by Dec 16, 2027.
Singlife said it generally does not disclose customer numbers for individual products.

The decision to discontinue Singlife Account is “part of our ongoing review of our product offerings to ensure they remain relevant to customers’ evolving financial needs”, said a Singlife spokesperson on Nov 18.

In an e-mail on Nov 16 at about 5pm, Singlife Account executive director Bernard Low notified existing customers of the account closure, providing details on what to expect from the changes. Customers also received a pop-up notification on their Singlife app.
Singlife will also stop accepting new account applications.

The closure date depends on the account value. Accounts with less than $100 will close on Dec 16, 2026. If the account has remained below $100 for more than 120 days as of Nov 11, 2026, it will close from Dec 16, 2026. If the 120-day mark is reached after Nov 11, 2026, the account will be closed in the following month.

Accounts with $100 and above will close on Dec 16, 2027. Until then, customers with at least $100 in their accounts can continue to make top-ups and withdrawals, earn the base rate of 1.5% per annum, and continue to be covered as long as their policy remains in force.

The insurance coverage bundled with the Singlife Account will lapse when the account is closed, but existing customers can still submit claims for insured events that occurred while the policy was in force.
From Dec 16, 2026, customers will no longer be able to make payments to third-party merchants using funds from the Singlife Account via PayNow UEN.

Customers can opt to withdraw their funds earlier, but the account will still close on its scheduled date. Singlife urged customers to make sure they have linked and updated their bank account details in the Singlife app to automatically return their remaining funds. If the refund process fails, customers will be contacted.
The discontinuation of Singlife Account does not affect customers who hold other insurance policies with Singlife.

Singlife was founded by former HSBC Insurance Singapore CEO Walter de Oude in 2014. He led Singlife’s acquisition and integration of Singlife with Aviva in 2020, before leaving the firm. He launched Chocolate Finance in 2024.

In several Reddit threads posted on Nov 16, some existing customers discussed alternatives to switch their cash to, laying out other options in the market, such as MariBank, GXS Bank, Trust Bank, Syfe, Chocolate Finance and SingFinance.

The Singlife Account, launched in 2019, is an insurance savings plan that functions much like a savings account, allowing customers to earn returns on their deposits with no lock-in period and fees. It also provides payment features, and death or terminal illness coverage of up to 105% of the account value.

In a media release announcing Singlife’s merger with Aviva Singapore in 2020, it reported that the Singlife Account hit 100,000 downloads within the first three months of launch, with customers entrusting almost $500 million through the product. It was also referred to as a “mobile-first” insurance savings plan.
At the time, customers could earn 2.5% interest per annum on their first $10,000 with an initial contribution of $500.
Singlife is now a wholly owned subsidiary of Sumitomo Life , a Japanese insurer based in Osaka.
“C ustomer needs have evolved, and we are focusing our efforts on developing solutions that better serve our customers,” said the firm spokesperson.

As demand for legacy planning solutions grows, the insurer recently introduced newer insurance savings plans, such as Singlife Heritage Income to help individuals preserve and distribute their wealth.

cna.headline: Thailand orders clean water for thousands facing arsenic pollution
cna.teaser: Thailand orders clean water for thousands facing arsenic pollution
fullText: BANGKOK: Thai authorities scrambled on Wednesday (Nov 18) to provide clean water for more than 20,000 households in the country's north affected by arsenic pollution linked to mining operations in neighbouring Myanmar.

Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul late on Tuesday ordered government agencies to find alternative water sources and closely monitor tap water quality in Chiang Rai province, said deputy government spokeswoman Lalida Persvivatana.

Tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended this month after officials found arsenic levels in the local waterworks to be 30 times higher than the safe limit.
The villages comprise more than 20,000 households, the government said.
Authorities have deployed two trucks to supply residents with clean drinking water, while the government is also considering alternative river water sources.

Researchers at Naresuan University said last week that chemical analysis and satellite modelling traced much of the arsenic-laden sediment in the Sai River to gold mining operations across the border in Myanmar.
Myanmar's long-running civil war enables unregulated exploitation of natural resources, including rare earth elements used in smartphones, wind turbines and electric vehicles.
Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow raised the issue of what he said was a "dramatic" increase in pollution in the Sai River during a visit last week to Myanmar to meet government officials.
He blamed "wastewater from mining", adding that it was an "urgent matter that needs urgent attention".
The Thai government says it has also discussed the issue with Beijing, with researchers saying many of the mining operations in Myanmar are Chinese-run.
There are fears the pollution is being washed far down the Mekong River, a waterway supporting millions of people across several countries.
Thai officials said arsenic had been found in the urine of 17 out of 177 people tested in October in the northeastern province of Nong Khai, on the border with Laos.

listening.title: Singapore Expands Electric Vehicle Charging Network in Public Housing
listening.transcript: Singapore is stepping up its green mobility efforts by installing thousands of new electric vehicle charging points across public housing estates. Officials state that providing convenient charging infrastructure is essential for encouraging drivers to switch from traditional petrol engines. Local residents have welcomed the move, though some note that parking spaces remain limited during peak hours. Urban planners expect the network to be fully operational by the end of next year.

economistArticle.title: The Enduring Lure of the Public Market
paras: In recent years, corporate commentators have repeatedly warned that public stock markets are losing their shine. Venture capital funds, sitting on vast dry powder, have allowed tech startups to stay private for longer than ever before. Regulatory compliance costs, regulatory scrutiny, and the relentless pressure of quarterly reporting are frequently cited as overwhelming burdens that deter founders from floating their companies.

Yet despite these complaints, the ultimate destination for high-growth tech firms remains remarkably consistent: an initial public offering. Private capital, for all its abundance, cannot substitute forever for the liquidity and prestige that public exchanges provide. Sooner or later, early investors demand an exit, and employees seeking to monetize their equity force the founder's hand.

Furthermore, the argument that stringent regulation acts as an insurmountable deterrent fails to hold up under scrutiny. While complying with disclosure rules and accounting standardisation is indeed expensive, it also serves as a crucial stamp of legitimacy. Institutional investors are far more willing to commit massive capital to firms whose financial statements are subjected to rigorous public oversight.

Public listing also grants companies a currency for acquisitions that private equity cannot easily replicate. Listed shares can be used directly as valuation units to acquire competitors, facilitating expansion without draining cash reserves. Moreover, the brand prestige of being listed on major exchanges remains an unmatched marketing tool for global expansion.

Ultimately, the choice to go public is delayed rather than abandoned. While regulatory burdens may alter the timing of a listing, they rarely alter the eventual outcome. For ambitious startups aiming to build enduring global institutions, the public market remains the indispensable proving ground.
economistArticle.cn:
近年来，企业评论家反复警告称，公开股票市场正逐渐失去吸引力。由于手里握着巨额未投资资金，风险投资基金使得科技初创公司能够比以往任何时候都维持更长时间的私有状态。合规成本、监管审查以及季度财报带来的无休止压力，常被指责为阻碍创始人将公司上市的沉重负担。

然而，尽管存在这些抱怨，高增长科技企业的最终归宿依然高度一致：首次公开募股（IPO）。尽管私人资本非常充裕，但它无法永远替代公开交易所提供的流动性和声望。早晚有一天，早期投资者会要求退出，而希望将股权变现的员工也会倒逼创始人做出选择。

此外，认为严格的监管构成了不可逾越之阻碍的观点在细究之下难以立足。尽管遵守信息披露规则和会计标准化确实成本高昂，但这同时也构成了至关重要的合法性认可。机构投资者更愿意将巨额资金投入到财务报表经过严格公开监督的企业中。

公开上市还为公司提供了收购交易中的“硬通货”，这是私募股权难以轻松复制的。上市公司股票可以直接用作估值单位来收购竞争对手，从而在不消耗现金储备的情况下促进扩张。此外，在主要交易所上市所带来的品牌声誉，对于全球扩张而言仍然是无与伦比的营销工具。

归根结底，去公开市场的选择只是被推迟了，而非被放弃。尽管监管负担可能会改变上市的时机，但它们很少能改变最终的结果。对于旨在打造持久全球性企业的雄心勃勃的初创公司而言，公开市场依然是不可或缺的试金石。

gems.s: Private capital, for all its abundance, cannot substitute forever for the liquidity and prestige that public exchanges provide.
gems.why: The sentence uses the prepositional contrast 'for all its [noun]' to gracefully acknowledge a counter-argument before delivering the primary thesis. 句子使用了 'for all its [名词]' 的介词让步结构，在阐述核心论点之前优雅地承认了对立事实。

gems.s: While regulatory burdens may alter the timing of a listing, they rarely alter the eventual outcome.
gems.why: This sentence employs antithesis through parallel structure ('alter the timing' vs 'alter the outcome') to make a concise and memorable conclusion. 该句通过平行结构（改变时机 vs 改变结果）运用了对照手法，使结论简洁有力且令人印象深刻。
